summary: Linux finite resources accept host-local workload profile keys across shell, Effect and KDL callers. The host freezes resource estimates before admission, generation controls enforce each member separately, and shell callers can atomically write terminal receipt files bound to the authenticated root execution and argv. Resources cancel requests authenticated cancellation and waits for confirmed retirement.

replay.detail: Keyed request replay preserves its accepted estimate instead of consulting a changed host seed. Historical raw requests and custody remain readable.

schema.detail: Optional profile, estimate and disk-path fields extend resource requests; shell executions retain root execution identity and canonical receipt subject. Historical reader arms remain authoritative.

rules.detail: Known keys reject caller resource overrides and caller-supplied estimates. Nested executions retain authenticated ownership and the frozen parent profile.

compatibility.detail: Adds --profile, positive --max-members, root-only --receipt-file, owner-scoped --request-id, --as selectors, --require-parent, --inherit-parent, request cancellation with seven-day tombstones, authenticated resources member-scope --exec-id, offline resources in-member --owner-uid, Effect profile/diskPath and KDL profile/disk-path. FRACTAL_RESOURCE_MEMBER_EXEC_ID identifies the current generation separately from the root receipt identity. New shell execution semantics require resource_profile_keys>=1. Raw no-key callers remain supported; unknown keys require complete raw declarations until caller cutover.

downtime.detail: No host deployment or caller cutover is activated by this change.

manual.detail: Configure workload seeds in the execution host finite_resources.profiles map before switching callers to known keys. Upgrade readers before publishing keyed declarations.

recovery.detail: Keep accepted request snapshots and historical custody through confirmed retirement. Do not rewrite active reservations when changing host seeds. Future request-class strings remain losslessly readable as unsupported classes, including in execution lists; they cannot be submitted or acquire admission on this host. Unsupported-class shell cancellation by execution or request ID is refused before changing the cancel flag. Program resource retirement rejects unsupported classes before cancelling linked child runs; background cleanup defers those records and continues supported work. Authority initialization skips unsupported admission observations with diagnostics, retains their membership rows, and marks observation coverage incomplete rather than failing schema validation; supported admissions can continue. Tests cover unknown-class roundtrip and mixed lists, rejected submission/admission/update/cancellation, unchanged synthetic membership after authority recovery, and unchanged live child status with no cancellation claims on rejected retirement. This does not certify complete E1 metadata preservation or a live E1-to-E0 rollback.
